title: 06 — Working with Iceberg: PyIceberg, Polars and DuckDB
html:
06 — Working with Iceberg: PyIceberg, Polars and DuckDB

The one idea: you do not need Spark to run an Iceberg lakehouse. PyIceberg creates tables, commits appends, overwrites, upserts and deletes, evolves schemas and tags snapshots from plain Python; Polars and DuckDB read the same tables for analysis. Everything in this chapter runs on a laptop.

1. Install

uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate          # or: python -m venv .venv
uv pip install "pyiceberg[pyarrow,pyiceberg-core,sql-sqlite,s3fs]" polars duckdb
Extra Why you need it
pyarrow Reading and writing Parquet, Arrow tables
pyiceberg-core Rust transforms — required to write to partitioned tables (month/bucket/…); without it append fails with NotInstalledError
sql-sqlite A SQLite-backed catalog for local experiments with no server
s3fs (or pyarrow S3) Object storage access for MinIO/S3

2. Connect to a catalog

2.1 Local, no server: SQL catalog

from pyiceberg.catalog.sql import SqlCatalog

catalog = SqlCatalog(
    "local",
    uri="sqlite:///warehouse/catalog.db",       # catalog state (table name -> metadata location)
    warehouse="file:///absolute/path/warehouse", # where data and metadata files go
)

2.2 REST catalog (Lakekeeper, Polaris, Unity Catalog …) on MinIO

from pyiceberg.catalog import load_catalog

catalog = load_catalog(
    "lake",
    **{
        "type": "rest",
        "uri": "http://localhost:8181/catalog",
        "warehouse": "demo",
        # Only needed when the catalog does not vend credentials:
        "s3.endpoint": "http://localhost:9000",
        "s3.access-key-id": "admin",
        "s3.secret-access-key": "password123",
        "s3.path-style-access": "true",
    },
)

Or keep configuration out of code in ~/.pyiceberg.yaml:

catalog:
  lake:
    type: rest
    uri: http://localhost:8181/catalog
    warehouse: demo

and call load_catalog("lake"). Environment variables of the form PYICEBERG_CATALOG__LAKE__URI work too.

3. Namespaces and tables

3.1 Create a namespace per layer

for ns in ("bronze", "silver", "gold"):
    catalog.create_namespace_if_not_exists(ns)

catalog.list_namespaces()            # [('bronze',), ('gold',), ('silver',)]
catalog.list_tables("silver")

3.2 Define a schema explicitly

Field IDs are permanent (chapter 05), so define them yourself for important tables:

from pyiceberg.schema import Schema
from pyiceberg.types import NestedField, StringType, DateType, DecimalType, IntegerType
from pyiceberg.partitioning import PartitionSpec, PartitionField
from pyiceberg.transforms import MonthTransform, IdentityTransform
from pyiceberg.table.sorting import SortOrder, SortField

schema = Schema(
    NestedField(1, "isin",        StringType(),        required=True),
    NestedField(2, "nav_date",    DateType(),          required=True),
    NestedField(3, "nav",         DecimalType(18, 4),  required=True),
    NestedField(4, "scheme_code", IntegerType(),       required=False),
    identifier_field_ids=[1, 2],          # the natural key — used by upsert
)

spec = PartitionSpec(
    PartitionField(source_id=2, field_id=1000, transform=MonthTransform(), name="nav_month"),
)
order = SortOrder(SortField(source_id=1, transform=IdentityTransform()))   # cluster by isin

nav = catalog.create_table(
    "silver.nav",
    schema=schema,
    partition_spec=spec,
    sort_order=order,
    properties={"write.parquet.compression-codec": "zstd"},
)

Shortcut for experiments: catalog.create_table("silver.nav", schema=arrow_table.schema) infers the schema from Arrow and assigns IDs.

3.3 Load an existing table

nav = catalog.load_table("silver.nav")
nav.schema(); nav.spec(); nav.sort_order(); nav.properties
nav.metadata_location           # the current *.metadata.json

4. Writing data

All writes take a pyarrow.Table. Build it with the table's own Arrow schema so nullability and types match — the most common error is "required field is nullable" when Arrow defaults every column to nullable.

from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal
import pyarrow as pa

arrow_schema = nav.schema().as_arrow()

batch = pa.Table.from_pylist([
    {"isin": "INF209K01YN0", "nav_date": date(2026, 10, 30), "nav": Decimal("123.4567"), "scheme_code": 119551},
    {"isin": "INF209K01YN0", "nav_date": date(2026, 10, 31), "nav": Decimal("124.0010"), "scheme_code": 119551},
    {"isin": "INF179K01BB8", "nav_date": date(2026, 10, 31), "nav": Decimal("55.1200"),  "scheme_code": 100123},
], schema=arrow_schema)

4.1 Append — add rows

nav.append(batch)        # one atomic commit -> one new snapshot (operation: append)

4.2 Overwrite — replace the rows matching a filter

from pyiceberg.expressions import EqualTo, And, GreaterThanOrEqual, LessThan

# Reload one month for one fund: delete matching rows and insert the batch, in ONE commit
nav.overwrite(
    batch,
    overwrite_filter=And(EqualTo("isin", "INF209K01YN0"),
                         GreaterThanOrEqual("nav_date", "2026-10-01"),
                         LessThan("nav_date", "2026-11-01")),
)

Without overwrite_filter, overwrite replaces the whole table.

4.3 Upsert — update matching keys, insert the rest

Uses identifier_field_ids (or pass join_cols=["isin", "nav_date"]):

fix = pa.Table.from_pylist(
    [{"isin": "INF179K01BB8", "nav_date": date(2026, 10, 31), "nav": Decimal("55.2100"), "scheme_code": 100123}],
    schema=arrow_schema,
)
result = nav.upsert(fix)
result.rows_updated, result.rows_inserted       # (1, 0)

In a bitemporal Silver table you would not upsert in place — you append a new version (chapter 09). Upsert suits current-state tables and Gold aggregates.

4.4 Delete

nav.delete(delete_filter=EqualTo("isin", "INE000000000"))

4.5 Several changes in one commit — transactions

with nav.transaction() as tx:
    tx.delete(delete_filter=EqualTo("isin", "INF209K01YN0"))
    tx.append(batch)
    tx.set_properties({"last_loaded_manifest": "01JBX7…"})
# committed atomically on exit; nothing is visible if an exception is raised

4.6 Writing from Polars

import polars as pl
df = pl.read_parquet("bronze_extract.parquet")
nav.append(df.to_arrow().cast(nav.schema().as_arrow()))   # cast to match types and nullability exactly

Recent Polars versions also offer df.write_iceberg(nav, mode="append").

4.7 Recording lineage on each commit

nav.append(batch, snapshot_properties={
    "source_manifest_id": "01JBX7…",
    "source_sha256": "9f2c…e41a",
    "pipeline_version": "1.4.2",
})

These land in the snapshot summary, so every version of the table says which file and code produced it.

5. Reading data

5.1 Scan with filters and projection

scan = nav.scan(
    row_filter=And(EqualTo("isin", "INF179K01BB8"), GreaterThanOrEqual("nav_date", "2026-10-01")),
    selected_fields=("isin", "nav_date", "nav"),
    limit=1000,
)
scan.to_arrow()          # pyarrow.Table
scan.to_polars()         # polars.DataFrame
scan.to_pandas()
scan.plan_files()        # which data files would be read — useful to check pruning

String filters work too: row_filter="isin = 'INF179K01BB8' AND nav_date >= '2026-10-01'".

5.2 Lazy scans with Polars

import polars as pl
lf = pl.scan_iceberg(nav)                 # or pl.scan_iceberg("s3://…/metadata/….metadata.json")
lf.filter(pl.col("nav") > 100).group_by("isin").agg(pl.col("nav").mean()).collect()

5.3 SQL with DuckDB

Two options:

# a) Hand a PyIceberg scan to DuckDB (uses PyIceberg planning and pruning)
con = nav.scan(row_filter="nav_date >= '2026-10-01'").to_duckdb(table_name="nav")
con.sql("SELECT isin, max(nav) FROM nav GROUP BY isin").show()

-- b) DuckDB's iceberg extension reading a metadata file directly
INSTALL iceberg; LOAD iceberg;
SELECT count(*) FROM iceberg_scan('s3://warehouse/silver/nav/metadata/00005-….metadata.json');

-- Newer DuckDB releases can ATTACH an Iceberg REST catalog and query tables by name
-- (check your DuckDB version's iceberg extension docs for the exact options)
ATTACH 'demo' AS lake (TYPE iceberg, ENDPOINT 'http://localhost:8181/catalog');
SELECT * FROM lake.silver.nav LIMIT 10;

6. Time travel, snapshots and tags

for s in nav.snapshots():
    print(s.snapshot_id, s.timestamp_ms, s.summary.operation)

nav.history()                                  # which snapshot was current, when
nav.current_snapshot().snapshot_id

# Read an old snapshot
old = nav.scan(snapshot_id=5247466366727240160).to_arrow()

# Tag a certified release — a named, durable pointer to this exact snapshot
snap = nav.current_snapshot().snapshot_id
nav.manage_snapshots().create_tag(snap, "vintage_2026_10_31").commit()

# Read by tag later
tagged = nav.snapshot_by_name("vintage_2026_10_31")
nav.scan(snapshot_id=tagged.snapshot_id).to_polars()

# Branches for write-audit-publish
nav.manage_snapshots().create_branch(snap, "staging").commit()
nav.append(batch, branch="staging")              # main is untouched
# … validate the staging snapshot, then point main at it (fast-forward) …

Verified behaviour: after an upsert corrected one NAV, reading the tag vintage_2026_10_31 still returned the original value 55.1200, while the current table returned 55.2100.

7. Evolving the table

from pyiceberg.types import StringType, LongType
from pyiceberg.transforms import BucketTransform

with nav.update_schema() as u:
    u.add_column("currency", StringType(), doc="ISO 4217")
    u.update_column("scheme_code", field_type=LongType())         # int -> long widening
    u.rename_column("scheme_code", "amfi_scheme_code")             # within one update, refer to the OLD name

with nav.update_spec() as s:
    s.add_field("isin", BucketTransform(8), "isin_bucket")         # new files also bucket by isin

with nav.transaction() as tx:
    tx.set_properties({"write.target-file-size-bytes": str(512 * 1024 * 1024)})

Old data files are not rewritten. Old rows read currency as null.

8. Inspecting a table

nav.inspect.snapshots()       # pyarrow tables you can turn into Polars
nav.inspect.files()           # every live data file with record counts and sizes
nav.inspect.partitions()
nav.inspect.manifests()
nav.inspect.refs()            # branches and tags
nav.inspect.history()

import polars as pl
files = pl.from_arrow(nav.inspect.files())
files.select(pl.len(), pl.col("file_size_in_bytes").mean() / 1e6)   # count and avg MB: small-file check

9. Maintenance from Python

PyIceberg's maintenance API is growing. Snapshot expiry is available:

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=30)
nav.maintenance.expire_snapshots().older_than(cutoff).commit()     # snapshots referenced by tags/branches are kept

For compaction and orphan-file removal at scale, run Spark procedures (rewrite_data_files, remove_orphan_files) or use your catalog's managed table maintenance. Check what your PyIceberg version supports before relying on it.

10. A complete Bronze → Silver load

from pyiceberg.expressions import EqualTo
import polars as pl

bronze = catalog.load_table("bronze.nav_raw")
silver = catalog.load_table("silver.nav")

def promote(manifest_id: str):
    raw = pl.from_arrow(bronze.scan(row_filter=EqualTo("manifest_id", manifest_id)).to_arrow())

    typed = raw.with_columns(
        pl.col("nav").cast(pl.Decimal(18, 4), strict=False),
        pl.col("nav_date").str.to_date("%d-%b-%Y", strict=False),
    )
    failed = typed.filter(pl.col("nav").is_null() | pl.col("nav_date").is_null() | (pl.col("nav") <= 0))
    passed = typed.join(failed.select("row_id"), on="row_id", how="anti")

    if failed.height:
        write_quarantine(failed, manifest_id)          # Postgres or an Iceberg quarantine table

    out = passed.select("isin", "nav_date", "nav", "scheme_code").to_arrow().cast(silver.schema().as_arrow())
    with silver.transaction() as tx:                   # all-or-nothing promotion
        tx.append(out, snapshot_properties={"source_manifest_id": manifest_id})

11. Common errors

Symptom Cause Fix
NotInstalledError: pyiceberg_core on append Partitioned table, missing Rust transforms Install pyiceberg[pyiceberg-core]
Mismatch in fields … required … optional Arrow column nullable, Iceberg field required Build/cast with table.schema().as_arrow()
CommitFailedException Another writer committed first Retry: reload table, re-apply, commit (PyIceberg retries some cases)
S3 AccessDenied / endpoint errors on MinIO Missing endpoint or path-style setting Set s3.endpoint and s3.path-style-access, or use catalog credential vending
Decimal precision error Value exceeds decimal(P,S) Widen precision in schema (safe evolution)

12. Questions to test yourself

  1. Why does PyIceberg require you to cast Arrow data to the table's schema before writing?
  2. What is the difference between overwrite with a filter and upsert? Which is idempotent if re-run?
  3. Write the code to tag the current snapshot and read it back a month later.
  4. How would you check that a filter on nav_date actually prunes files?
  5. Implement write-audit-publish using a staging branch.

13. Review checklist

  • Schemas declared with explicit field IDs and identifier fields for key tables.
  • Writes cast to table.schema().as_arrow().
  • Multi-step changes use one transaction.
  • Each commit carries source manifest and pipeline version in snapshot properties.
  • Certified releases tagged; snapshot expiry scheduled.
